title: At 75 and 63, They Married at the Bilaspur Old-Age Home Where They Met
excerpt: Kanhaiya Lal, rescued from a forest after his wife's death, and Sabina, who reached Himachal from Kolkata with no one to claim her, wed at Apna Ghar in Dayoli on November 25 — and will now move to a new home in Nalagarh together.
body:
• Kanhaiya Lal, 75, and Sabina, 63, residents of the Apna Ghar old-age home in Dayoli, Bilaspur, married there on Wednesday, November 25, with traditional rituals.
  • Kanhaiya Lal, from Thunag village in Mandi district, lost his wife, lived for a time in a forest, and was rescued and brought to the home in 2022.
  • Sabina, originally from Kolkata, reached Shimla a few years ago and spent about four years at Nari Niketan in Mashobra before moving to the Bilaspur home.
  • After the wedding, the couple will move to a new old-age home in Nalagarh so they can live together.

Kanhaiya Lal, 75, and Sabina, 63, both residents of Apna Ghar Old Age Home in Dayoli, in the Ghaghas area of Bilaspur district, tied the knot there on Wednesday, November 25, in a ceremony their fellow residents helped celebrate.

Kanhaiya Lal, a native of Mandi district, wore a sherwani, while Sabina, originally from Kolkata, dressed in a red saree, and the two exchanged wedding vows in accordance with traditional wedding rituals, The Times of India's report of the ceremony said. The couple exchanged garlands around 11:30 a.m., followed by the traditional rituals. The celebrations had begun on Tuesday evening with the haldi ceremony, at which women residents of the home applied turmeric to the bride and groom and sang traditional wedding songs. Before the rituals, the couple completed a court marriage in Bilaspur.

Bilaspur Deputy Commissioner Kiran Bhadana attended the ceremony on Wednesday, congratulated the newlyweds and presented them with a shagun. District Welfare Officer Ramesh Bansal and Apna Ghar founder Prakash Bansal were among those present.

Two hard roads to Dayoli

Kanhaiya Lal, a resident of Thunag village in the Seraj area of Mandi district, has been staying at the old-age home for nearly three years. After his wife's death, a distressed Kanhaiya Lal started living in a forest before being rescued and brought to the old-age home in 2022, officials said. Accounts of his earlier years say he had no children and had transferred his land to his brothers before ending up in the forest.

Sabina's road was longer. Originally from Kolkata, she reached Shimla a few years ago while travelling. Police took her to Nari Niketan in Mashobra, near Shimla, where she stayed for about four years; at first she was unable to provide details about herself because of her mental condition. After her condition improved, she was shifted to the Dayoli old-age home and decided to stay at the institution, Prakash Bansal said.

"Their acquaintance at the old-age home gradually developed into a relationship, with both deciding to spend the rest of their lives together."

— Prakash Bansal, founder, Apna Ghar Old Age Home

A first for the home, and a new home together

Advocate Prakash Chand Bansal, who founded and runs Apna Ghar, said it was the first time at the home that two elderly residents had become life partners. After the wedding, the couple will shift to a newly established old-age home in Nalagarh, run by the Manav Seva Trust, so that they can begin their married life together in a home of their own. For two people whose families and past lives had fallen away — one rescued from a forest, the other found far from her home city with no way to say who she was — the wedding was, as the reports from Dayoli put it, companionship found late, and chosen deliberately.
image_caption: Kanhaiya Lal and Sabina in wedding dress at Apna Ghar Old Age Home in Dayoli, Bilaspur, on November 25, 2026. The two residents of the home married there after meeting as fellow residents.
nri_angle: A story about companionship and care in old age that resonates with diaspora families supporting elderly parents back in India.
author: Diaspora Desk
